title: Look and feel (UX)
intro: Your 13 UX principles turned into concrete choices, plus theme, fonts and states. Principles 8, 9 and 11 (4 px spacing grid, line and letter spacing, lighter outer and stronger inner shadows) are built as you wrote them.

questions.question: How should colour be used across the app?

options.label: Teal brand, four status colours (Recommended)
options.description: MONAI teal #00C0B5 only for the brand and main buttons; green done, amber waiting, red blocked, violet needs a person, each with its own icon.

options.label: Teal also means done
options.description: Teal replaces green for complete items; fewer colours, but brand and status can be confused.

options.label: A new palette
options.description: Move away from teal to a fresh brand colour set chosen with you.

questions.why: Principle 10 (colour with purpose). Today teal is a fill only with dark text on it (DESIGN 1.9), every text colour is at 4.5:1 or better on white, violet already marks 'needs review'; U10: status chips by colour only. MONAI theme set by Eswar for V1.

questions.question: Which font family should the new interface use?

options.label: Keep Atkinson Hyperlegible (Recommended)
options.description: Made for easy reading, with clearly different 1 / l / I and 0 / O (useful for IDs and values); already self-hosted; Latin script only.

options.label: Noto Sans family
options.description: Covers Hindi, Tamil, Kannada and other Indian scripts in one matching look; needed if R01 adds Indian languages.

options.label: Inter
options.description: A common modern interface font; letter shapes less distinct than Atkinson's.

questions.why: Today Atkinson Hyperlegible and JetBrains Mono are self-hosted under static/tb/fonts (SIL OFL 1.1). Text in Indian languages needs Indic fonts, so this follows R01 (languages).

questions.question: How should dark mode be offered?

options.label: Light default, dark by choice (Recommended)
options.description: Everyone starts light; anyone can switch in their profile (radiologists reading in dark rooms may like it).

options.label: Follow the device setting
options.description: Dark when the phone or PC is dark; nothing to choose, but the look changes between devices.

options.label: Light only for now
options.description: One theme to build and test; dark later.

questions.why: No dark theme exists today (tb.css has no dark rules). A light room screen usually reads better in a lit meeting room. Every status colour must pass contrast in both themes.

questions.question: How dense should the working screens be?

options.label: Roomy, 16 px text (Recommended)
options.description: Bigger text and rows on the 4 px grid; fewer items per screen, easier on tired eyes and phones.

options.label: Compact desktop, roomy phone
options.description: More rows on the OPD desktop, larger touch targets on phones.

options.label: Compact everywhere
options.description: Most on one screen (15 px text as today); harder to read.

questions.why: Principles 8 and 9 (let text breathe, spacing in steps of 4 px, line spacing). Today body text is 15 px with paddings off the grid (10 px, 14 px); U01: text-heavy screens.

questions.question: How should buttons and actions be labelled?

options.label: Icon and word, mostly (Recommended)
options.description: Clinical actions show an icon and a short word (Send, Waive); only universal ones (copy, call, close, search) are icon alone.

options.label: Icon and word everywhere
options.description: Clearest; buttons take more room on phones.

options.label: Icons alone with tooltips
options.description: Cleanest look; a doctor must learn or hover to know an icon, and phones have no hover.

questions.why: Principle 7 (visual hierarchy, icons rather than text). U01: screens are text-heavy today. A wrong tap matters for clinical actions, so a word next to the icon removes doubt. Icons from one self-hosted open set (for example Lucide, ISC licence).

questions.question: Phones and the room screen have no hover: how should tappable things show they can be tapped?

options.label: Look tappable, hint on tap (Recommended)
options.description: Buttons look like buttons, tappable rows end in a small arrow, an (i) icon opens a short hint on tap; desktop hover only adds to this.

options.label: Hover tooltips plus long-press
options.description: Tooltips on desktop hover; on phones a long-press shows the same hint.

options.label: Short hint text under controls
options.description: Small grey lines always visible; nothing hidden, but more text on screen.

questions.why: Principle 6 (affordances and signifiers: hover, tooltips). U01: help is explained three times today (paragraph, help line, long tooltip).

questions.question: Which form fields should come pre-filled with the usual choice?

options.label: Logistics only (Recommended)
options.description: Fetch window 12 months, the next board date, hospital level and the doctor's department; cancer and stage group always picked by the doctor.

options.label: Logistics plus my last choices
options.description: The same logistics, but each doctor's last-used values (fetch window, level, board) are remembered; cancer and stage group are still picked every time.

options.label: Logistics plus usual cancer
options.description: Also pre-selects the department's most common cancer; faster, but a wrong pick changes the required records.

questions.why: Principle 1 (defaults that feel like a recommendation). Scope: the stage group (NCG setting) is picked by the doctor from the signed reports and the system never works out a stage, so clinical choices are not pre-filled. The 12-month fetch window is already the default (V2 decisions). Settled: each treating doctor has at least one resident.

questions.question: Principle 2 (anchoring a price against a bigger number) is about pricing: where should it be used?

options.label: Pricing and pitch only (Recommended)
options.description: Hospital pricing and the Healthathon deck compare the cost with a bigger figure (for example a deferred case); clinical screens show plain facts.

options.label: Also a monthly time card
options.description: The coordinator's dashboard shows time spent in Vaidyx per Case File beside a published manual figure (about 13 min, Hartmann 2026).

options.label: Also on each Case File
options.description: Each Case File shows its own preparation time beside that published figure.

questions.why: Principle 2. Clinical screens must not carry performance or accuracy claims; a published figure with its source is the honest anchor. Time in Vaidyx can be counted from the audit log.

questions.question: What should a new user get on first login, before being asked for anything more?

options.label: A check of one patient (Recommended)
options.description: Type one UHID and see the records fetched and what is missing in seconds; profile details after; short hints on first use instead of a tour.

options.label: A ready demo Case File
options.description: A finished synthetic Case File to explore, plus a skippable 4-step tour.

options.label: A short tour, then the home
options.description: 4 screens explaining the parts of the app; nothing done for them yet.

questions.why: Principle 3 (gift first, like Duolingo) and the onboarding tour. For a supporting doctor the gift is their open requests, already listed. Today: a '3 steps to start' card on the home (UI_PLAN C.3). Account steps at first login come from R04; on the public demo the patient is synthetic.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R04-Q11 (what a new user sees first); its 'check one patient' option was added to R04-Q11.

questions.question: Which look-and-feel choices should the profile set-up offer, so people make the app their own?

options.label: Theme and text size (Recommended)
options.description: Light or dark (if R18-Q03 offers dark) and normal or large text, seen live while choosing.

options.label: Pin what my home shows
options.description: Choose and order the home's cards (to-do, board date, requests).

options.label: Accent colour
options.description: A personal colour for the menu bar only; status colours never change.

questions.why: Principle 4 (IKEA effect: ask more than email and password, such as name and theme). Identity fields (name, title, photo) come from R04 (profile fields); these are the look-and-feel ones.

questions.topic: Progress that does not start at 0
questions.question: Principle 5 says progress should not start at 0: how should that work honestly?

options.label: Count what the system did (Recommended)
options.description: A new Case File already shows 'records fetched' and 'check run' as done, so it starts near a third with no made-up numbers.

options.label: Head start outside clinical bars
options.description: Set-up and profile bars start at 20%; the Case File readiness bar stays exact.

options.label: Steps instead of percent
options.description: '3 of 7 done' with ticks; no percentage anywhere.

questions.why: Principle 5. Readiness decides whether a Case File goes to the board (R07), so its bar must never overstate completeness; counting real automatic steps gives the momentum honestly.
questions.notes: Dropped in validation (17 Oct): same as R07-Q04 (an honest readiness bar that does not start at 0) and R04-Q10 (set-up progress).

questions.question: When a list is empty or something fails, what should the screen show?

options.label: Plain line, cause, one action (Recommended)
options.description: In place, not a pop-up: 'The hospital system did not answer.' with a Try again button; technical details under 'Details'.

options.label: Small picture, line and action
options.description: The same with a friendly illustration; warmer, takes more room.

options.label: Note at the bottom only
options.description: A short pop-up note that fades (today's way); easy to miss.

questions.why: Principle 12 (a response for every state, error pages included). Button states (default, hover, pressed, disabled, loading) are built for every button as you wrote. U08: spinners that never stop, no screen-reader announcements, double submits; UI_PLAN item 5: empty states with a next step.

questions.question: How should a 15 to 35 second AI step (summary, specialty brief) look while it runs?

options.label: Live steps, free to leave (Recommended)
options.description: Each step shows as it happens (reading records, writing, checking quotes); the doctor can leave and is alerted when it is ready.

options.label: Preview filling in
options.description: Grey placeholder lines turn into sentences only once each is written and its quote verified.

options.label: Spinner with time estimate
options.description: 'About 30 s'; simple, nothing to read meanwhile.

questions.why: K02: summary 24 to 34 s, brief 13 to 17 s, a question median 6 s, GPU capped at 300 W. Principle 12. No option shows an unverified sentence as fact. The alert channel comes from R14.

questions.question: After a small action (copy, send, save), how should the app confirm it?

options.label: Button change plus slider (Recommended)
options.description: The button turns into 'Copied' or 'Sent' with a tick and a small slider confirms it at the bottom for 2 seconds; also announced to screen readers.

options.label: Button change only
options.description: The confirmation sits where the finger is; nothing slides in.

options.label: Slider only
options.description: Your example: a small 'Copied' slider; the button itself does not change.

questions.why: Principle 13 (small responses everywhere, such as a 'copied' slider). U08: today's pop-up notes are not announced to screen readers. Destructive actions keep confirmation and undo (T15, kept).
